captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a thrust ball bearing assembly consisting of a flat, ring-shaped retainer cage and ten spherical balls. The retainer cage has a wide, circular ring profile with a central open hole. Ten evenly spaced spherical balls are embedded within the ring, protruding slightly from both the top and bottom faces to allow rolling contact.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric thrust ball bearing assembly in OpenSCAD. The user should be able to adjust the rolling radius (R), the number of balls (N), and the wall width (W), with the ball size automatically calculated to fit the geometry.
captions.factory: The design is built using a difference operation on a main cylinder to create the ring-shaped cage. The cage ring is defined by subtracting a smaller concentric cylinder from a larger one. A loop is used to distribute spherical cutouts around the ring at a calculated radius 'r' to form the bearing pockets. Finally, a separate loop places smaller, solid spheres (with a radius reduced by the wall thickness 'W') within the pockets to represent the rolling ball bearings.
